highlights: AI agents are doing our shopping for us, and wreaking havoc on the internet. You wake up to a notification that a grocery-store employee will deliver all of the ingredients for the three recipes you saved last night to your “Weeknight Dinner” folder. While you brew your coffee, a program browses online retailers to compare toilet-paper prices, and another solicits competitive bids for Sheetrock work you need done in the garage. On your lunch break, you get an alert that computers acting on your behalf noticed some unclaimed funds and class-action payouts in a state database and claimed them. By the time you get home, the groceries are on your doorstep, and you’ve gotten back $150. This is the future that OpenAI, Meta, xAI, Google, and the rest are selling with a spate of always-on AI assistants that work for you. highlights: # TSMC's net profit hits record in third quarter. TAIPEI (AFP) -- Taiwanese chip giant TSMC said Thursday that net profit soared to another record high in the third quarter, buoyed by massive global demand for AI hardware. The result marked the sixth straight record quarterly net profit for the company, the world's biggest contract maker of microchips, including those used in Nvidia AI data center processors. TSMC's net profit for July-September surged 68.7 percent year-on-year to NT$763.1 billion ($23.6 billion), beating analyst estimates of NT$739.5 billion. "Every leading AI chip still runs through its factories, so for investors, this week's results are about as close as it gets to a health check on the entire AI build-out." Fears over AI's dangers have intensified in recent weeks, leading to calls for leading US labs to deliberately slow down their technological advancement.

"And now our researchers and the model work hand in hand to make the next version of the model," he said during the roundtable, which Google shared on Wednesday. In a safety report for its new Argon model, Google said that some components of the AI research and development cycle were getting automated.
